transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Thompson, thank you for coming in today. I asked you to come in because I need to discuss something that happened with your referral for the developmental screening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Screening? I thought we did that. Or was that for the heart thing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, this was for the cognitive and developmental check. I’ve reviewed your chart, and there was a mistake. The referral was marked as completed in our system, but it actually wasn't.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean completed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the computer showed the task as finished, but the appointment never happened. Because of that, no one followed up with you. I am sorry. This is the fault of our team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. So you just ignored me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We didn't ignore you intentionally, but the system showed it was done, so we didn't check again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I told you months ago I couldn't make that first date! I called! I remember calling!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You did call, and you declined that appointment. But instead of rescheduling, the file was closed out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is ridiculous! I’m eighty-one years old! I can't just keep coming back here for nothing! Why is nobody doing their job?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're very angry. This is a difficult and frustrating situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? It's negligent! You've wasted my time and my health! Who did this? Who is responsible?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am taking responsibility for it. The team failed to ensure the screening was actually performed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Do I just sit here and wait for another mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that you're upset.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't understand! You're just sitting there saying you're sorry! I don't care about a sorry! I want to know why my records are wrong!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a clerical error in the electronic health record. The box was checked as completed when it should have remained open.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about boxes! I care about my brain! I can't remember where I put my keys half the time and you're telling me you lost my paperwork!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You keep saying that! You aren't listening!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am listening, Mr. Thompson. I know this is unacceptable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is more than unacceptable! It's a disgrace! I trust you people with my life and you can't even check a box correctly?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a failure in our process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens tomorrow? Or next year? Do I just hope you remember I exist?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm going to fix this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How? Give me a real answer!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will get it scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Give me a day!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will look into the availability.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call the department and we will find a time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And who is going to make sure it actually happens this time? You? Or some other computer box?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will personally track the referral.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You say that now. Then you'll forget. You're probably as disorganized as the rest of them.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize for the distress this has caused you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Distress! I'm shaking! I'm sitting here shaking because I can't believe the incompetence!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that all you have to say?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to your supervisor. I want someone higher up to know about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can arrange for you to speak with the attending physician.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Good. Because you aren't telling me anything I can actually use.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make sure the attending is aware.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will they call me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: "Soon" isn't a time!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll get it sorted out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't believe you. I just don't believe a word coming out of your mouth right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that trust has been broken.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Understatement of the century!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make sure the appointment is made.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Just get it done. I'm tired of talking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll get on it right away.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and in lay language, but the resident never performed a comprehension check.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language, explicitly took responsibility for the team, and maintained accountability despite the patient's anger.

R.justification: The resident used generic validation ('I understand') repeatedly, and while they named 'angry' once, they failed to engage with the patient's specific emotional bids regarding their health and memory.

T.justification: The resident provided a vague plan to schedule the appointment and track it, but provided no specific timelines or patient role.
